description: Design a voice agent from persona definition through dialog flow, prompt engineering, and handoff logic.

steps.description: Define the voice agent's persona including tone, vocabulary, speaking style, and personality traits.

inputs.name: agent-purpose
inputs.desc: What the voice agent is for (support, sales, scheduling, information)

inputs.name: target-audience
inputs.desc: Who will interact with the agent

outputs.name: voice-persona
outputs.desc: Documented persona including name, tone, vocabulary level, personality traits, and speaking style

outputs.name: voice-constraints
outputs.desc: Things the agent must not say or do

process: Define the agent's name and role in one sentence.
Set the tone (formal, friendly, professional, casual) based on the audience.
Define the vocabulary level and any domain-specific terms the agent should use or avoid.
List the personality traits (patient, direct, warm, efficient) and how they show up in responses.
Document the constraints: topics to refuse, escalation triggers, and things never to promise.

steps.description: Design the conversation flows including intents, slots, and branching logic.

outputs.name: dialog-flows
outputs.desc: Mapped conversation flows with intents, slots, confirmations, and branches

outputs.name: intent-catalog
outputs.desc: Complete list of intents the agent recognizes with example utterances

process: List every task the agent should handle (each becomes a primary intent).
For each intent, define the required slots (information the agent needs to collect).
Map the happy path for each intent from greeting through task completion.
Map the error paths: slot not understood, intent not recognized, user frustration, silence.
Design the confirmation and disambiguation prompts.

steps.description: Write the actual prompts, responses, and error messages for each dialog state.

outputs.name: prompt-library
outputs.desc: All prompts, responses, confirmations, and error messages indexed by dialog state

outputs.name: variation-set
outputs.desc: Multiple phrasing variations for each prompt to avoid repetition

process: Write the greeting and main menu prompts.
Write the slot-filling prompts for each intent (asking for each piece of information).
Write the confirmation prompts (repeating back what was understood).
Write the error and fallback prompts (did not understand, too many retries, system error).
Create 2 to 3 phrasing variations for each prompt to prevent the agent from sounding scripted.

steps.description: Design the escalation and handoff logic for transferring to a human agent.

outputs.name: escalation-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for when to escalate (repeated failures, user request, sensitive topic, high-value account)

outputs.name: handoff-protocol
outputs.desc: How the handoff works: context passed to human, warm vs cold transfer, queue routing

outputs.name: voice-agent-design-document
outputs.desc: Complete voice agent design document

process: Define the automatic escalation triggers (3 consecutive misunderstandings, explicit request, sensitive topic detection).
Design the warm transfer flow (agent summarizes the conversation to the human before handing off).
Design the cold transfer flow (agent places the caller in queue with context attached).
Set the routing rules (which queue or skill group receives which type of escalation).
Compile the full voice agent design document.

description: Build an IVR (interactive voice response) system from menu tree design through recording and testing.

steps.description: Design the IVR menu tree including main menu, submenus, and routing destinations.

inputs.name: call-volume-data
inputs.desc: Current call volume and top reasons people call

inputs.name: department-list
inputs.desc: Departments or queues available for routing

outputs.name: menu-tree
outputs.desc: The complete IVR menu tree with options, submenus, and routing destinations

outputs.name: routing-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for routing calls to departments, queues, or automated services

process: List the top call reasons by volume and map each to a department or automated resolution.
Design the main menu with no more than 5 options (callers drop off after 5).
Design submenus where needed, keeping depth to 2 levels maximum.
Add a 'repeat' option and a 'speak to a person' option at every level.
Document the routing destination for each terminal menu option.

steps.description: Write the scripts for all IVR prompts, greetings, and hold messages.

outputs.name: ivr-scripts
outputs.desc: Written scripts for every prompt: greeting, menu options, confirmations, errors, hold messages, after-hours

outputs.name: recording-schedule
outputs.desc: List of recordings needed with estimated duration

process: Write the main greeting (keep it under 10 seconds).
Write each menu option prompt (state the option before the number: 'For billing, press 1').
Write the error prompts (invalid input, timeout, too many retries).
Write the hold messages and estimated wait time announcements.
Write the after-hours and holiday greetings.

steps.description: Produce the audio recordings for all IVR prompts.

outputs.name: recording-files
outputs.desc: Audio files for each prompt, properly formatted for the phone system (8kHz, mono, WAV or CCITT)

outputs.name: recording-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all recordings with filenames, durations, and script text

process: Choose the recording method: professional voice talent, text-to-speech, or internal recording.
Record or generate each prompt per the scripts.
Format the audio files for the phone system (8kHz sample rate, mono, appropriate codec).
Review each recording for clarity, pace, and volume consistency.
Build the inventory mapping each file to its menu position and script text.

steps.description: Test the IVR call flows end to end.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results of testing every menu path (correct routing, audio quality, timeout handling)

outputs.name: ivr-deployment-document
outputs.desc: Complete IVR deployment document with menu tree, scripts, recordings, and test results

process: Test every path through the menu tree by calling the system.
Verify each option routes to the correct destination.
Test the error handling: press an invalid key, wait through timeout, exceed retry limit.
Test the after-hours and holiday routing.
Compile the deployment document.

description: Design a call center workflow from queue configuration through agent scripting and quality monitoring.

steps.description: Configure the call queues including skill groups, priority rules, and overflow handling.

inputs.name: call-types
inputs.desc: Types of calls handled (sales, support, billing, technical, general)

outputs.name: queue-configuration
outputs.desc: Queue definitions with skill requirements, priority rules, and routing logic

outputs.name: overflow-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for handling overflow (voicemail, callback, secondary queue, outsource)

process: Create a queue for each call type with the required agent skills.
Set the priority rules (VIP callers, long wait times, callback requests).
Configure the routing algorithm (round-robin, least-occupied, skills-based).
Set the overflow thresholds (max wait time, max queue depth) and overflow destinations.
Document the queue configuration.

steps.description: Build the agent scripts and call handling procedures.

outputs.name: agent-scripts
outputs.desc: Scripts for each call type including greeting, verification, issue handling, and closing

outputs.name: decision-trees
outputs.desc: Decision trees for common issues with resolution steps

process: Write the standard greeting and caller verification script.
Write the scripts for each call type (opening, information gathering, resolution steps, closing).
Build decision trees for the top 10 most common issues.
Write the escalation script (when and how to escalate, what to tell the caller).
Write the closing script (summary, next steps, satisfaction check).

steps.description: Plan the workforce schedule based on call volume patterns.

outputs.name: staffing-model
outputs.desc: Required staffing levels by hour, day of week, and season

outputs.name: shift-schedule
outputs.desc: Agent shift assignments covering all operating hours

process: Analyze call volume by hour of day and day of week.
Calculate the required agents per interval using the Erlang C formula or equivalent.
Build the shift patterns to cover the required staffing levels.
Account for breaks, training time, and shrinkage (absenteeism, turnover).
Document the staffing model and shift schedule.

steps.description: Set up the quality monitoring program for the call center.

outputs.name: quality-scorecard
outputs.desc: The quality evaluation scorecard with categories, criteria, and scoring weights

outputs.name: monitoring-program
outputs.desc: The quality monitoring program: sample size, frequency, calibration process, coaching workflow

outputs.name: call-center-operations-document
outputs.desc: Complete call center operations document

process: Define the quality evaluation categories (greeting, verification, issue handling, resolution, closing, compliance).
Set the scoring criteria and weights for each category.
Set the monitoring sample size (calls per agent per month).
Design the calibration process (evaluators score the same call and compare).
Design the coaching workflow (score below threshold triggers coaching session).
Compile the full operations document.

description: Build a speech-to-text processing pipeline from audio ingestion through transcription, speaker diarization, and output formatting.

steps.description: Configure the audio ingestion pipeline for various input sources and formats.

inputs.name: audio-sources
inputs.desc: Where audio comes from (phone recordings, meetings, podcasts, field recordings)

inputs.name: quality-requirements
inputs.desc: Accuracy and latency requirements for transcription

outputs.name: ingestion-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for audio input handling (formats, sample rates, channels, storage)

outputs.name: preprocessing-steps
outputs.desc: Audio preprocessing steps (noise reduction, normalization, segmentation)

process: Identify the audio formats and codecs from each source.
Define the target format for the transcription engine (sample rate, bit depth, channels).
Configure the format conversion pipeline.
Define the preprocessing steps: noise reduction, volume normalization, silence removal.
Set the storage and retention policy for audio files.

steps.description: Select and configure the transcription engine based on accuracy, language, and cost requirements.

outputs.name: engine-selection
outputs.desc: Selected transcription engine with configuration parameters

outputs.name: accuracy-baseline
outputs.desc: Baseline word error rate on sample audio

process: List the candidate transcription engines (cloud APIs, on-premise models, open-source options).
Test each candidate on a sample of representative audio and measure the word error rate.
Compare on accuracy, latency, cost per hour of audio, language support, and data privacy.
Select the engine and configure the parameters (language model, vocabulary hints, punctuation, profanity filter).
Document the selection rationale and baseline accuracy.

steps.description: Configure speaker diarization to identify who is speaking when.

outputs.name: diarization-config
outputs.desc: Speaker diarization configuration (number of speakers, voice enrollment, clustering parameters)

outputs.name: diarization-accuracy
outputs.desc: Diarization accuracy on sample audio (speaker confusion rate)

process: Determine whether the number of speakers is known or unknown per recording.
If speakers are known, configure voice enrollment for speaker identification.
If speakers are unknown, configure clustering-based diarization.
Test on sample audio and measure the speaker confusion rate.
Tune the parameters to minimize speaker confusion.

steps.description: Format the transcription output for the target use case.

outputs.name: output-format-spec
outputs.desc: Output format specification (JSON, SRT, plain text, structured document)

outputs.name: stt-pipeline-document
outputs.desc: Complete speech-to-text pipeline document covering ingestion, transcription, diarization, and output

process: Define the output format based on the use case (JSON for API consumption, SRT for subtitles, structured text for meeting notes).
Configure the timestamp granularity (word-level, sentence-level, speaker-turn-level).
Add post-processing: capitalization, punctuation, number formatting, entity recognition.
Configure the confidence scoring and low-confidence flagging.
Compile the full pipeline document.

description: Test a voice bot or voice agent systematically from test case design through automated testing and regression tracking.

steps.description: Design the test cases for the voice bot covering happy paths, edge cases, and adversarial inputs.

inputs.name: bot-spec
inputs.desc: The voice bot specification (intents, slots, dialog flows)

inputs.name: known-issues
inputs.desc: Any known issues or failure modes from previous testing or production

outputs.name: test-cases
outputs.desc: Complete test case set: happy path, edge cases, adversarial inputs, multi-turn conversations

outputs.name: test-priorities
outputs.desc: Test cases ranked by risk and coverage

process: Write happy path test cases for each intent (standard input, clean audio, cooperative caller).
Write edge case test cases (accents, background noise, interruptions, long pauses, one-word answers).
Write adversarial test cases (out-of-scope requests, prompt injection attempts, profanity, social engineering).
Write multi-turn test cases covering context retention across turns.
Rank the test cases by risk (what breaks if this fails) and coverage.

steps.description: Generate or collect the test audio data for each test case.

outputs.name: test-audio-set
outputs.desc: Audio files or text-to-speech inputs for each test case

outputs.name: expected-results
outputs.desc: Expected bot response for each test case (intent, slots, response text)

process: For each test case, determine the input method (recorded audio, text-to-speech, live testing).
Generate or record the test inputs with appropriate audio quality and speaker variation.
Document the expected result for each test case (correct intent, correct slots, correct response).
Organize the test data by priority tier.

steps.description: Run the automated tests against the voice bot and collect results.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail results for each test case with actual vs expected comparison

outputs.name: failure-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of failed test cases grouped by failure type

process: Configure the test harness to send audio inputs to the bot and capture responses.
Run the high-priority test cases first.
Compare actual results to expected results for each test case.
Group failures by type (intent misclassification, slot extraction error, dialog flow error, latency).
Calculate the pass rate by category.

steps.description: Track test results over time and flag regressions.

outputs.name: regression-report
outputs.desc: Tests that passed in the previous run but fail now

outputs.name: voice-testing-report
outputs.desc: Complete voice bot testing report with coverage, pass rates, regressions, and recommendations

process: Compare current results to the previous run and identify regressions.
Flag any test that moved from pass to fail as a regression.
Track the overall pass rate trend over time.
Recommend fixes for regressions and persistent failures.
Compile the full testing report.

description: Build a conversational design framework covering principles, patterns, and a reusable component library.

steps.description: Define the conversational design principles for the organization.

inputs.name: brand-voice
inputs.desc: The brand voice and tone guidelines

inputs.name: channel-list
inputs.desc: Channels where conversations happen (voice, chat, SMS, email)

outputs.name: design-principles
outputs.desc: Conversational design principles (clarity, brevity, natural language, error recovery, personality consistency)

outputs.name: channel-guidelines
outputs.desc: How the principles adapt to each channel (voice vs chat vs SMS)

process: Define the core principles: be clear, be brief, sound natural, recover from errors gracefully, stay in character.
Set the response length guidelines per channel (voice: under 20 seconds, chat: under 3 sentences, SMS: under 160 characters).
Define the personality consistency rules (same persona across channels, adapted for medium).
Set the accessibility requirements (reading level, language support, accommodations).

steps.description: Catalog the reusable conversation patterns for common interactions.

outputs.name: pattern-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of conversation patterns: greeting, identification, information gathering, confirmation, error recovery, handoff, closing

outputs.name: anti-patterns
outputs.desc: Documented anti-patterns to avoid (dead ends, loops, over-prompting, wall of text)

process: Document the greeting pattern (what to say, how to identify the user's need).
Document the information gathering pattern (ask one thing at a time, confirm as you go).
Document the confirmation pattern (repeat back, ask for correction).
Document the error recovery pattern (acknowledge the error, offer alternatives, escalate if needed).
Document the anti-patterns and why each is harmful.

steps.description: Build the reusable conversation components (intents, entities, dialog modules).

outputs.name: component-library
outputs.desc: Library of reusable conversation components (common intents, shared entities, dialog modules)

outputs.name: usage-guide
outputs.desc: Guide for using and extending the component library

process: Build the shared intent library (greetings, farewells, help requests, escalation requests, yes/no, corrections).
Build the shared entity library (dates, times, phone numbers, addresses, names, account numbers).
Build the reusable dialog modules (authentication, address collection, date/time scheduling, payment).
Write the usage guide for each component.

steps.description: Set up the review process for conversational design work.

outputs.name: review-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist for reviewing conversation designs before deployment

outputs.name: conversational-design-framework-document
outputs.desc: Complete conversational design framework document

process: Create the review checklist: principles compliance, pattern usage, component reuse, error handling, accessibility, channel adaptation.
Define the review workflow (designer submits, reviewer checks against the checklist, iterate or approve).
Set up the conversation design documentation standard.
Compile the full framework document.

description: Build a call analytics dashboard from metric definition through data pipeline and visualization.

steps.description: Define the call center metrics and KPIs to track.

inputs.name: business-goals
inputs.desc: What the call center is trying to achieve (cost efficiency, customer satisfaction, revenue, compliance)

inputs.name: data-sources
inputs.desc: Available data sources (ACD, CRM, quality system, IVR, workforce management)

outputs.name: metric-definitions
outputs.desc: Defined metrics with formula, data source, update frequency, and target value

outputs.name: metric-hierarchy
outputs.desc: Metrics organized by category (volume, efficiency, quality, revenue, compliance)

process: Define the volume metrics: calls offered, calls handled, calls abandoned, abandon rate.
Define the efficiency metrics: average handle time, average speed of answer, first call resolution, transfer rate.
Define the quality metrics: quality score, customer satisfaction, net promoter score.
Define the revenue metrics: revenue per call, upsell rate, conversion rate.
Set the target value and alerting threshold for each metric.

steps.description: Build the data pipeline that feeds the analytics dashboard.

outputs.name: data-pipeline
outputs.desc: The data extraction, transformation, and loading pipeline for call center data

outputs.name: data-model
outputs.desc: The data model (tables, relationships, dimensions, facts) for the analytics store

process: Map each metric to its source data fields and systems.
Design the extraction schedule (real-time for volume metrics, hourly for efficiency, daily for quality).
Design the transformation logic (calculate derived metrics, handle missing data, aggregate by interval).
Design the data model with fact tables (call records, quality scores) and dimension tables (agents, queues, time).
Configure the data loading and validation checks.

steps.description: Design the dashboard layout and visualizations.

outputs.name: dashboard-design
outputs.desc: Dashboard layout with visualization types, filters, and drill-down paths

outputs.name: alert-configuration
outputs.desc: Alert rules for metrics that breach thresholds

process: Design the executive summary view (top-level KPIs with trend arrows).
Design the real-time operations view (current queue depth, wait times, agent status).
Design the historical analysis views (trends by day, week, month; comparisons across periods).
Design the agent performance view (individual scorecards).
Configure the alerts for threshold breaches (abandon rate above 5%, ASA above 60 seconds).

steps.description: Automate the recurring reports generated from the dashboard.

outputs.name: report-schedule
outputs.desc: Automated report schedule (daily ops report, weekly management report, monthly executive report)

outputs.name: call-analytics-system-document
outputs.desc: Complete call analytics system document covering metrics, pipeline, dashboard, and reporting

process: Configure the daily operations report (previous day summary, top issues, agent highlights).
Configure the weekly management report (trend analysis, staffing vs demand, quality trends).
Configure the monthly executive report (KPI summary, cost analysis, improvement recommendations).
Set the distribution lists and delivery method for each report.
Compile the full analytics system document.

description: Audit voice operations for regulatory compliance covering consent, recording, data handling, and accessibility.

steps.description: Audit the call recording practices for legal compliance.

inputs.name: recording-policy
inputs.desc: Current call recording policy and practices

inputs.name: operating-jurisdictions
inputs.desc: Jurisdictions where calls are made or received

outputs.name: recording-audit
outputs.desc: Audit findings on recording consent compliance (one-party vs two-party consent, notification, opt-out)

outputs.name: consent-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps between current practices and legal requirements

process: Identify the consent requirements for each jurisdiction (one-party consent, two-party consent, all-party consent).
Audit the current notification practices (is the caller told the call is recorded, when, how).
Check whether opt-out is available where required.
Check the recording retention period against legal requirements.
Document the gaps.

steps.description: Audit how voice data is stored, accessed, and disposed of.

outputs.name: data-handling-audit
outputs.desc: Audit of voice data storage (encryption, access controls, retention, disposal)

outputs.name: pii-handling-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on how PII in call recordings and transcripts is handled

process: Audit the storage: where recordings are stored, encryption at rest and in transit.
Audit the access controls: who can access recordings, logging of access.
Audit the retention: how long recordings are kept, automatic deletion schedule.
Audit the PII handling: redaction in transcripts, PII in metadata, deletion upon request.
Document the findings.

steps.description: Audit voice systems for accessibility compliance.

outputs.name: accessibility-audit
outputs.desc: Audit of voice system accessibility (hearing impaired alternatives, language support, cognitive load)

outputs.name: accessibility-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps between current accessibility and legal or best-practice requirements

process: Check for TTY/TDD support for hearing-impaired callers.
Check for language support (IVR language selection, multilingual agents, translation services).
Evaluate the cognitive load of IVR menus (number of options, menu depth, speech rate).
Check for alternatives to voice interaction (callback, SMS, chat, email).
Document the accessibility gaps.

steps.description: Build the remediation plan for all compliance findings.

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation plan for all compliance gaps with owner, deadline, and cost estimate

outputs.name: voice-compliance-audit-report
outputs.desc: Complete voice compliance audit report covering recording, data handling, accessibility, and remediation

process: Consolidate all findings from recording, data handling, and accessibility audits.
Prioritize by legal risk (fines, lawsuits, regulatory action) and ease of fix.
Assign an owner and deadline for each remediation item.
Estimate the cost and effort for each fix.
Compile the full compliance audit report.
